subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What static capability taxonomy, grant storage, and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw expose for skill/tool permissions?
rationale: The remaining work changes security semantics and public plugin/skill contracts; automation cannot choose the right default-deny upgrade behavior, grant persistence model, or declared-versus-enforced trust wording safely.

options.title: Stage capability grants in core
options.body: Approve a phased core/plugin-API plan: schema and diagnostics first, then explicit grants, pre-model filtering, execution-boundary checks, and durable audit records.

options.title: Limit core to audit metadata
options.body: Keep only inspect/status metadata in core and require governance plugins or ClawHub policy to enforce runtime decisions.

options.title: Pause until related PRs settle
options.body: Defer this umbrella until the audit-only permissions PR and narrower descriptor/RFC issues establish a stable vocabulary.

recommendation.title: Stage capability grants in core
recommendation.body: Approve a phased core/plugin-API plan: schema and diagnostics first, then explicit grants, pre-model filtering, execution-boundary checks, and durable audit records.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent's recent history is closest to the plugin manifest and hook contract surfaces that would define the public capability/grant API.
